Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (integration + rate limits)

Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Goal: prototype Redwood inference for Acme's search reranker + chat assistant by end of August.
- Integration focus: SDK setup, auth (API key rotation + scoped keys), request routing for region/latency, structured output + tool-calling for the assistant, embeddings + reranker flow.
- Rate limiting: you surfaced target QPS ~25 user-facing requests/sec, burstier batch jobs at night (up to 200 QPS). You also asked about 429s, retries, and idempotency for deduping sensitive ops.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share a short SDK quickstart and a recommended rate-limit/retry pattern for your platform. (attached)
2) Can your infra lead share the acceptable retry policy (max attempts, overall timeout) and whether you require idempotency tokens for user-facing calls?
3) Schedule a short architecture call with your API team and our inference lead — 30 minutes to walk routing/auth and embedding storage.

I've attached the SDK quickstart and a one-pager on rate-limit patterns. If that looks good, I'll loop in Rishi for the architecture session.

Thanks,

Thanks Ben — that recap is perfect. A few answers from our side: 

- Retry policy: for user-facing requests we prefer exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 attempts, and a 10s overall timeout. For background batch jobs we can be more aggressive, but we'd like to avoid unbounded retries.
- Idempotency: yes, for any side-effecting operations we need idempotency tokens. For the reranker pipeline itself (read-only scoring) we don't need tokens, but for any create/update ops (e.g., storing re-ranker results back to our db) we do.
- We'll need guidance on how you recommend surfacing 429 vs 503 vs 4xx to clients, and what headers you return for quota remaining / reset.

I'll bring Priya (infra) and our api-team alias to the next call. Proposed time: Thurs 10am PT?

Alex

alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (integration + rate limits)

Alex — great, Thurs 10am PT works. I'm attaching two short notes here inline: 1) recommended rate-limit + retry patterns and 2) SDK auth/routing quickstart. Full attachments are also included.

Rate-limit & retry recommendation (summary):
- Edge rate limits: per-API-key / per-tenant token with a soft limit and a hard limit. Soft limit returns 429 with Retry-After header, hard limit returns 429 and an alert to operators.
- Response headers we set: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch sec), Retry-After (seconds).
- Retry strategy (client): for 429/503 use exponential backoff with full jitter; base backoff 200ms, max backoff 8s, max attempts 5. Abort early on 4xx (non-retriable).
- Idempotency: include Idempotency-Key for any non-idempotent call (POST that writes). We persist per-key for 24 hours to dedupe. Server returns 409 if duplicate with referencing header X-Idempotency-Status.

SDK quickstart & auth: 
- Use our official Node/Python SDKs which handle automatic retries and idempotency key injection if you pass requestId.
- Auth: api-key with scoped permissions; we also support short-lived OAuth tokens for service accounts. Key rotation: recommend per-service key (not global), rotate daily/weekly per your policy.
- Routing: pass region hint in request header X-Region-Hint or use an endpoint per-region (us-east, eu-west). SDK defaults to region-aware endpoints if you set tenant region.

Embeddings & reranker pattern (short):
1) Compute embeddings via /embeddings endpoint; include requestId for dedupe.
2) Store embeddings in your vector DB.
3) For reranking: retrieve candidates, call Redwood scoring endpoint (stateless, idempotent) with candidate IDs and context. This endpoint is rate-limited separately from generation endpoints.

I'll add Rishi on the call to walk through KV cache, batching, and structured output/tool-calling considerations. See attachments.

Ben

From: Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (integration + rate limits)

Thanks — a couple of follow-ups from infra: 

1) For server-side idempotency, we have a dedicated request-store with 72h retention. If Redwood only persists 24h, we need to understand the duplication window implications. Would you be able to accept a longer idempotency token TTL (we can pass a token created by our system)?

2) How do you recommend handling long-tail latency for streaming responses (assistant uses streaming for UI). If a stream is interrupted and client retries, can the SDK resume from last token or do we need to restart?

3) For quota headers: do you expose per-model quotas or only per-account? We'd like per-route quotas so our routing can fallback to cheaper model variants automatically.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Rao
Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
